utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Case number IT-97-25-PT, the Prosecutor against the accused Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: If it please the Court. Dirk Ryneveld, along with Peggy Kuo and George Huber, and we're prepared to proceed this morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am Mihajlo Bakrac, a lawyer, and I represent the accused Krnojelac. This time I'm alone in representing my client. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, are you able to hear the proceedings in a language which you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Yes, Your Honour, I can follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, this is a Status Conference called as required by the Rules. Whether there's any particular matter that you want to raise, I don't know. I've certainly received no notice of any. Are there any matters that the Prosecution wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: The only thing, Your Honour, is that I've had a very brief discussion with my learned friend, and in terms of the ongoing attempt to perhaps talk about admissions, and the other aspect, of course, is getting a statement from the accused, an interview, he indicates that those matters will all await, of course, the fact that we're still awaiting the decision on the Defence challenge to the amended indictment. So that is the only outstanding matter that I understand is, at the moment, left to resolve before my friend and I can get on with the matters of an interview of the accused, for example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I'm very sorry about that delay. There was a draft almost completed, I think, at the end of November when events of December and three hearings got away from us. But it should be finished shortly, and in any event bearing in mind that Judge Cassese is retiring at the end of the month, it has to be delivered before then. But I think it shall be delivered well before then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So you'll be able to get on with those matters. Now, Mr. Bakrac, are there any matters from your point of view that you want to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I completely agree with what my learned friend the Prosecutor has just stated. We discussed the matter prior to the Status Conference and matters are as they stand. I don't think there will be any impediment to further agreement and to speeding up the case once we receive a response to our motion. I have no further questions on my part. I have talked to the accused as to whether there are any matters we could discuss at this Status Conference, but he has none to offer at this present point in time, unless he says otherwise. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do you want to speak to him about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have already talked to him. I talked to him before the start of the Status Conference, and that's why I say that I'm speaking on his behalf, and we agreed that we would await the decision and then continue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. I will adjourn this Status Conference. If there are any other applications to be made, you should put them in by way of a motion. The judgement will be given as soon as we can possibly do so, and I apologise again for the delay. I'll adjourn.
